questions.stem: Why can you hear someone talking around a corner but not see them?

options.text: Sound waves have a wavelength similar to the size of doorways, so they diffract significantly
Sound waves are longitudinal and light waves are transverse

questions.explanation: Sound waves have wavelengths of roughly 0.02 m to 17 m, which is similar to the size of doorways and corridors. This means sound diffracts significantly around corners. Light has a very small wavelength (around 500 nm), far smaller than a doorway, so it barely diffracts.
